```{r}
#| include: false
#| 
# Process dealer data
# Limit dataset to 2000-report year
dealer <- dealer %>% 
  filter(Year >= 2000 & Year <= RptYr)

# Weight - Length relationships for BET and swordfish
# Equation W=a*L^b
# Swordfish: a=1.299x10^(-5) and b=3.0738  Lf=143.6cm and Lm=102cm
SW_L50_kg_f <- (1.299*10^(-5))*(143.6^3.0738)
SW_L50_kg_m <- (1.299*10^(-5))*(102^3.0738)
# Convert from Length to weight using Phoebe's numbers for the Hawaii fishery (gives weight in grams)
# Bigeye: L=103cm from Farley et al. 2018 (WCPFC scientific committee report on age and growth of BET)
BET_L50_kg <- round(0.0187*(103^2.9605))/1000  # these numbers are from phoebe

# Parse out bigeye and swordfish datasets (bigeye is deep set only, swordfish is shallow set only)
dealerBE <- dealer[which(dealer$SPECIES_FK == 6 & dealer$SET_TYPE == 'D'),]
dealerSW <- dealer[which(dealer$SPECIES_FK == 11 & dealer$SET_TYPE == 'S'),]

```

```{r}
#| include: false

# Set colors for species
allColor <- nmfs_palette('regional_alt1')(6)[2]
betColor <- nmfs_palette('coral')(4)[3]
swoColor <- nmfs_palette('alert_orange')(4)[4]

# Function to make a ridge plot
ridgefunc <- function(dealerDat, col, L50, L50col, xmax, xmin=0, cutoff=0.01, overlap=2, alpha=0.8, bwidth=2) {
  # Get the total number of fish sold each year
  numSold <- aggregate(NUM_SOLD ~ Year, data=dealerDat, FUN=sum)
  numSold$pretty <- prettyNum(c(numSold$NUM_SOLD), big.mark=",")

  # Make the ridge plot
  rdg <- ggplot(dealerDat, aes(x=WholeWeight, y=Year, group=Year)) + 
    stat_density_ridges(scale = overlap, 
                        rel_min_height = cutoff, 
                        quantile_lines = T, quantiles = 2, 
                        fill=col, alpha=alpha, bandwidth=bwidth
                        ) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = L50, color=L50col, linetype='dashed') + 
    scale_y_reverse(limits=c(RptYr+0.2, 1998.5), expand=c(0,0), breaks=seq(RptYr, 2000,by=-1)) + 
    theme_ridges(center_axis_labels = T) + 
    xlim(xmin,xmax) +
    xlab('Round Weight [kg]') + 
    ylab(NULL) +
    geom_text(data=numSold, aes(label=paste0('n = ', pretty), x=Inf, y=Year), hjust = 1, vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  
  return(rdg)
}

# make figures and save as objects
i <- ridgefunc(dealer, col=allColor, L50=-10, L50col=NA, xmax=90, xmin=-5, cutoff=0.02, alpha=0.8)
j <- ridgefunc(dealerBE, betColor, BET_L50_kg, L50col='gray', xmax=105, bwidth=2, alpha=0.8)
k <- ridgefunc(dealerSW, swoColor, c(SW_L50_kg_f, SW_L50_kg_m), 'gray40', xmax=310, xmin=-10, alpha=1, overlap=2, bwidth=10) # try binwidth=10 as well
```

```{r}
#| include: false

#--------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate Climatology of weight distribution for all fish, bigeye and swordfish 
#--------------------------------------------------------
# Bin all fish larger than 200kg
# All Fish
dealerSAFE <- dealer
dealer[which(dealer$WholeWeight >= 200), 'WholeWeight'] <- 200
dealerClim <- dealer[which(dealer$Year <=2009),]
dealerYr <- dealer[which(dealer$Year == RptYr),]
# Bigeye
dealerBE[which(dealerBE$WholeWeight >= 200), 'WholeWeight'] <- 200
dealerBEClim <- dealerBE[which(dealerBE$Year <= 2009),]
dealerBEYr <- dealerBE[which(dealerBE$Year == RptYr),]
# Swordfish
dealerSW[which(dealerSW$WholeWeight >= 200), 'WholeWeight'] <- 200
dealerSWClim <- dealerSW[which(dealerSW$Year <= 2009),]
dealerSWYr <- dealerSW[which(dealerSW$Year == RptYr),]

# Using function and plot to make density plots
histFunc <- function(datClim, datYr, color, img, ymin, ymax, xlab=NULL) {
  # Get the number of fish for each
  nClim <- prettyNum(c(sum(datClim$NUM_SOLD)),big.mark=',')
  nYr <- prettyNum(c(sum(datYr$NUM_SOLD)),big.mark=',')

  # Proportion of fish (counts/total counts)
  ggplot() + 
    geom_histogram(data=datClim, aes(x=WholeWeight, y=after_stat(count)/sum(after_stat(count))), fill='gray70', color='gray50', binwidth = 5) +
    geom_histogram(data=datYr, aes(x=WholeWeight, y=after_stat(count)/sum(after_stat(count))), fill=color, color=color, binwidth = 5, alpha=0.6) + 
    theme_bw() + 
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) + 
    scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) + 
    scale_x_continuous(expand = F) +
    xlab(xlab) +
    ylab('Proportion of Fish') + 
    annotate(geom='text', x=160, y=Inf, label=as.expression(bquote(n[climatology] == .(nClim))), vjust=2, parse=TRUE, size=3) + 
    annotate(geom='text', x=160, y=Inf, label=as.expression(bquote(n[.(RptYr)] == .(nYr))), vjust=4, parse=TRUE, size=3) +
    annotation_raster(img, xmin = 150, xmax = 170, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax) +
    geom_point()
  
}

pAll <- histFunc(dealerClim, dealerYr, allColor, beye, ymin=0.5, ymax=0.53) # dummy locations becuase time
pBE <- histFunc(dealerBEClim, dealerBEYr, betColor, beye, ymin=0.14, ymax=0.165)
pSW <- histFunc(dealerSWClim, dealerSWYr, swoColor, sword, ymin=0.11, ymax=0.13, xlab='Weight (kg)')
plotStack <- pAll / pBE / pSW + plot_layout(heights = c(1,1,1.05))
```

\
**Rationale:** Fish size can be impacted by a number of factors, including climate. Currently, the degree to which the fishery’s target species are impacted by climate, and the scale at which these impacts may occur, is largely unknown. Ongoing collection of size structure data is necessary for detecting trends in community size structure and attributing causes of these trends. Understanding trends in fish size structure and how oceanographic conditions influence these trends is an area of active research.\
\
**Status:** For the longline fishery as a whole, fish were larger than average in `r RptYr`, with a lower proportion of fish smaller than about 15 kg. Bigeye tuna were smaller than average in `r RptYr` with a median weight of `r signif(median(dealerBE$WholeWeight[which(dealerBE$Year == RptYr)], na.rm=T),4)` kg, the lowest during the period of record. Swordfish were much smaller than the previous years with a median weight of `r signif(median(dealerSW$WholeWeight[which(dealerSW$Year == RptYr)], na.rm=T),4)` kg, the lowest during the period of record and well below the L~50~ weight of 55.5 kg for female swordfish. The large proportion of small fish and the low median weight in `r RptYr` of both bigeye tuna and swordfish suggest a recruitment pulse into the fishery.\
\
**Description:** The weight of individual fish moving through the Honolulu auction is available from 2000 through the present. Using these weights, community size structure is presented. A standardized pooled climatological distribution (2000–2009) is presented, as is the `r RptYr` distribution. Similar distributions for target species (bigeye tuna and swordfish) are also presented. Annual time series of pooled target species weights are presented as ridge plots. Bigeye weights are from deep sets (≥ 15 hooks per float) only. Swordfish weights are from shallow sets (≥ 15 hooks per float) only. The Honolulu auction reports weights for gilled and gutted fish. A conversion factor is used to calculate the whole fish weights used for this indicator [@Langley2006-if].\
\
**Timeframe:** Annual.\
\
**Region:** Hawaiʻi-based longline fishing grounds.\
\
**Measurement Platform:** *In-situ* measurement.\
\
**Sourced from:** @PIFSCUnknown-no, @PIFSCUnknown-ke and the Hawaiʻi Division of Aquatic Resources, @Farley2018-ty, @Langley2006-if, and @Kapur2017-ho
